walkthroughs.body_html:
Inflation means the average price of stuff rises.

In 2000 a Freddo cost 10p. Today it's around 25–30p.

That isn't only Cadbury — most prices rise over time. 🍫

The UK uses the CPI — Consumer Prices Index.

Each month, the ONS prices a basket of goods (food, fuel, clothes, services) and compares it with last year. The percentage change = inflation. 🧺

If your wages don't rise as fast as prices, you can afford less — your purchasing power falls.

Falling prices (deflation) sounds nice but can stop people spending, hurting jobs.

mcqs.q: Are monopolies always bad for consumers?
options: Standard theory says monopolies restrict output and raise prices, but possible benefits include economies of scale, R&D investment and dynamic efficiency.
Monopolies are illegal and always harmful.
A Pigouvian tax is a tax only on rich people.
A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between GDP and GNP?
options: A monopoly is when one country dominates world trade.
GDP measures output produced within a country's borders; GNP measures output produced by a country's nationals wherever they are.
GDP is income and GNP is spending.
GDP and GNP are the same thing with different names.
